hero-description: Interactive experience of our documentary film on South Korean rurality
hero-add: In collaboration with Dong-Eui University of Busan
s1-sub: Recueil is a two-dimensional project: a 30-minute documentary film on South Korean rurality, and an interactive web experience that extends the film.
s1-p1: The film explores what rurality in South Korea looks like today: its realities, its demographic decline, and whether it truly still exists. It is anchored in the village of Sannae and the Buddhist temple Silsangsa, around which the Indra's Net community gravitates — a Buddhist community whose role in sustaining rural life is questioned.
s1-p2: On the site, users can choose to watch the film directly, or live the interactive experience: a map divided into two chapters, where each clickable area leads to a segment of the film, followed by a supplementary page enriching the narrative with data, figures and contextual elements — a way to go deeper than the film alone.
s1-p3: We were a team of 7 French students and 4 Korean students.
s1-p4: → I was in charge of the site design and illustrations.
s1-p5: I also oversaw the site's development and handled part of the sound recording during filming.
s2-p1: Before departure, the team conducted research to choose the subject and understand the issues of South Korean rurality, which guided the choice of Sannae-myeon and the Silsangsa temple as the film's anchor. The trip itself lasted three weeks, with most of the time based at Dong-Eui University in Busan, for pre-production, post-production and site development.
s2-p2: Four days were devoted to on-location filming. The language barrier was real. Making contact with members of the Indra's Net community, getting their agreement to film, finding moments of spontaneity — all of this required time, patience and listening. We eventually shared a meal at the temple with them, a moment that was for me one of the most powerful of the project.
img2-caption: Photos taken during filming at Sannae-myeon
s3-p1: The site design evolved in parallel with the film editing: the two fed each other. The art direction refined itself over rushes, editorial intentions, and what the film was truly becoming.
s3-p2: I created all the site's illustrations, including a hand-drawn map representing the Sannae-myeon region, reworked as a clickable SVG for navigating the web documentary.
s3-p3: The site also features a multilingual FR/EN/KR system and ambient sound to extend the immersion beyond the film.
s4-p1: This project was an extraordinary experience: three weeks in South Korea, documenting a subject I didn't know, in a language I don't speak.
s4-p2: What I take away professionally is the ability to design under uncertainty. The design, illustrations and site had to continuously adapt to a film that was being built at the same time.
